title: the bus roster finds a device by its name in any case, so mail from or to 'CC' reaches the cc shim
intention: Roster.shim_for resolves a device name case-folded against the fitted device ids (system_word.canon), so 'CC', 'Cc' and 'cc' all find the device folder cairn/devices/cc on a case-sensitive filesystem; a name that is no fitted device in any case still returns None and the bus still bounces it.
why: Observed 2026-11-14 by the orchestrator on the Dell: a codemother queueme bounced 54 times in one burst and each bounce raised a trouble whose text reads "the sender CC could not take the returned letter (no shim answers to 'CC' - a device's bus presence IS cairn/devices/CC/shim.py on disk, and nothing was discovered there)". The device folder is cairn/devices/cc and the roster looks a name up verbatim (Roster.shim_for -> _load_device_shim -> fitted_device_ids membership), so 'CC' finds nothing on Linux. System words fold case (Akien's standing rule; cairn.tools.system_word.fold). Every bounce to a sender named CC therefore cannot land and becomes a trouble: loud (Law 7 holds) but a flood from one avoidable cause. No existing ticket or question owns it (grep of tickets and questions, 2026-11-14).
traces_to: Law 7 (a bounce that cannot land is loud, and here avoidably so), Law 1 (case folding of system words is settled), and the standing rule that system words fold case via cairn.tools.system_word.
how: In Roster.shim_for, before the held/disk/discovered lookups, canonicalise name with system_word.canon over fitted_device_ids(root) and use the canonical id for the lookup and the hold; an unmatched name is passed through unchanged. Proof on a scratch tree with a device folder cc, case-sensitive on Linux, red first.

clauses.claim: Roster.shim_for('CC') returns the same shim as shim_for('cc') on a case-sensitive filesystem, so a bounce addressed to CC lands
a name that is no fitted device in any case (e.g. 'nobody') still returns None, so an undeliverable mail still bounces and raises its trouble

decisions.text: D1: the fold lives in Roster.shim_for through the published system_word tool; the bus server's hold_name is unchanged and keeps raising LookupError for a truly unknown name.
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; it is red only on a case-sensitive filesystem, so it is measured on Linux (the Dell), and Windows records it NOTRUN.

measured.saw: bus server.py hold_name raises LookupError 'no shim answers to <name>' and _raise_undeliverable_bounce (server.py ~432) raises the trouble with 'the sender X could not take the returned letter'; Roster.shim_for looks the name up verbatim; the device folder is cairn/devices/cc. A grep of tickets and questions for the sender-CC bounce found no owner. The orchestrator reported 54 bounces in a 0.2 s burst.
measured.how: read cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py hold_name and _raise_undeliverable_bounce, cairn/tools/bus_client/roster.py shim_for, and the bounce trouble text in the orchestrator's message; grep of CairnCommons/tickets and questions

measured.saw: Measured by the orchestrator on the Dell: bounce envelope 38460dafd9f842b8969b827dff502606, original_verb machines/orient/queueme, raised by CodeMotherShim at 2026-11-13T00:18:13Z, sender exactly 'CC'; `ls cairn/devices` there shows only `cc` (lowercase) and no CC folder. So the sender is the cc device written in another case: the assumption in assumption_check holds. Roster.shim_for was not called live; the Linux proof run is the behavioural measurement.
measured.how: orchestrator's cross-session message 2026-11-14: read the bounce envelope's sender on the Dell and ls cairn/devices
